(b) chunk 34 line 480, 'The M5 lecture *Hooks always fire* names that property' — 'M5' shorthand is established by chunk 10 (line 209) and recurs at chunks 12, 15, 17, 22, 29 before chunk 34; additionally named by its own italicized title in the same sentence, the strongest form the rule asks for. Chunk 34 line 480 names its source by module AND exact italicized title in one sentence ('The M5 lecture *Hooks always fire*'), not by position. Chunk 37 line 566 names both source files by literal filename in backticks, immediately adjacent to what each does. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two instances of the same mischaracterization, both pre-existing (outside the pinned diff, so not caught by any diff-scoped pass): chunk 15 line 282, 'M6 authors a second one, the learning-loop skill built from the two-session diff'; chunk 22 line 347-348, 'Your second authored skill from M6 is a strong candidate to wire into a schedule like this one.' Checked M6's own module body (`curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md`): its 'What You'll Learn' LO reads 'Generalize the shapes you mapped into a handoff prompt that builds your workflow skills across your stack' (not 'author a second skill'), its Key Concepts read 'The handoff prompt IS the loop. It packages the stack-map into a move that authors the skill each shape calls for, when you run it' (skill-authoring happens LATER, cold, off-session, when the student runs the prompt on their own time — not live during M6), and its deliverable table names the artifact 'Workflow-skills handoff prompt', not a skill. `grep -n 'second skill\|author.*skill' curriculum/lectures/the-loop-has-a-name.md` (M6's compound lecture) -> 0 hits; the phrase 'the learning-loop skill' as a named artifact appears nowhere in M6's own files. Harm: this is exactly rule 3's target shape (sibling of check_writing.md §15a) — a reader treats 'M6 authors a second [skill]' as a beat to expect and finds a handoff prompt instead, the same category of mismatch as a dead beat reference, just described-wrongly rather than deleted. No maintainer accept-note covers this claim.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Both instances: replace 'a second [authored] skill' framing with what M6 actually delivers — a handoff prompt that authors workflow skills later, when run cold. Do not invent 'the learning-loop skill' as a proper noun; M6's own files never name one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a lookup surface by its own lede ('Flat look-up for the primitives AE101 leans on. No pedagogy, no hand-holding.', line 3), so the per-slide bold-COUNT budget is waived by §9's own reference-page exception. The handle-cap sub-clause ('bold the label, not the sentence after it') still binds, and the file's dominant pattern — one bolded lead SENTENCE per prose entry (`grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*' body.txt` -> 23 spans over 6 words, e.g. line 91 'A rule with no `paths:` is not a lesser CLAUDE.md.' at 11 words, line 388 at 11 words) — is whole-sentence bolding, not label bolding, which reads as exactly the shape the carve-out's own wording tries to exclude. Not filed as REVISE: the two diff-touched instances (chunks 10, 13, 14, 34) only SHORTENED their bold spans and this pattern is pre-existing across the whole file, unmoved by this diff; the fix (rewriting ~20+ topic sentences into label+prose pairs) is a corpus-wide rewrite, not a narrow one, and the compendium's own text records an identical seam being explicitly declined as a REVISE on two other files on 2026-08-12/13 with the rule's carve-out written in direct response. Logged as a todo for the maintainer rather than re-litigated as a gate.
